faults.quote: Here's an exhibit: Roasted chickpea snacks — Economics of one bag and first-year launch costs.
faults.why: The candidate asked only for chip cost of goods and gross-margin history. The chickpea economics exhibit went out against that ask; it is simply the next data in sequence.

faults.quote: What would you want to know to judge whether the launch can realistically reach that in year one?
faults.why: This "that" dangles. It sits right after the line about chip SKU volume, but it apparently means the 6 million breakeven bags.

faults.quote: You're treating 6 million bags as reachable by comparing it to a revenue percentage.
faults.why: In answer to the interviewer's own question, the candidate said they wanted to know how many stores the line could get into. The case holds this (retailer_support, channels), yet the turn gives no release, refusal or deferral.

faults.quote: I can share the survey on shopper purchase intent and planning assumptions if you'd like.
faults.why: The candidate had not asked for survey or intent data; this offer was volunteered.

faults.quote: An exhibit for you — Proposal — In-store sampling program (first year of the launch). How do you read this exhibit?
faults.why: The candidate said they wanted to confirm chip contribution per bag. The case doesn't hold it, but no refusal was given; the turn moved straight to the next exhibit.

faults.quote: How would you guard against that?
faults.why: The candidate's last answer had already given mitigations: locking retailer commitments first and staging the marketing spend on a 12-week velocity read.
